search_log.query: Viṣṇu Purāṇa Book 4 chapter 19 ANU Taylor Raudrāśva Bharata Dvimīḍha genealogy
search_log.outcome: Read the ANU Press chapter text for the remaining named descendants. Used verse-level locators checked against the verse-indexed Sanskrit chapter. Added only explicit parentage or other stated relationships; unnamed members of collective lists were excluded.

search_log.query: Viṣṇu Purāṇa 4.19 Sanskrit verse sequence 1 and 5–15
search_log.outcome: Cross-checked the verse sequence and passage boundaries against the Sanskrit text with verse-level presentation. Where the two presentations vary in name forms or detail, retained the ANU wording and did not merge homonyms.

notes: This batch is separate from genealogy_scale.json. The prior batch already covers Puru through Bharata’s main descent and some names in Raudrāśva’s line; this file adds the remaining Raudrāśva sons and the other named branches in chapter 19.

ANU translation and the verse-indexed Sanskrit presentation show some variant spellings and genealogical differences. Claims follow the ANU translation’s wording; the secondary verse-indexed page is used for passage locators only, not as a reason to normalize variant identities.

Homonyms across branches are given different IDs. In particular, the Ajamīḍha-branch Kaṇva and Medhātithi are separate from Apratiratha’s Kaṇva and Medhātithi; Dvimīḍha-branch Sumati and Kṛta are separate from other namesakes. Bharadvāja and Vitatha are one node because this chapter expressly calls Bharadvāja Vitatha.

The Bharadvāja birth episode involves Bṛhaspati, Dīrghatamas, Mamatā and the Maruts, but this batch adds no biological parentage edge for Bharadvāja because the passage intertwines semen, birth and the Maruts’ presentation of the child to Bharata. The recorded relation to Bharata is explicitly a gift/son relation.
